keyFindings.description: Window 2 is still open: record's drop test (:347) assumes the clock local holds only rises, but record writes every non-removal entry's clock unconditionally (:356). answer (:642-647) records clocks it read by EncodeUpdate earlier, and touched's Meta reads (:737-739) can record late too, so a stale entry lowers local[X] from the return's c+1 back to c (and puts the old state in the batch). A removal at c then passes `c < c` false, deletes local[X] and replaces the batch entry; the other processes, still holding c, accept a null at an equal clock and drop a reader who is in the room.

Regression from the new drop test: when a purge frees the tombstone before the snapshot, the removal stands at local[X] read when touched began (:731), which can be behind a heartbeat recorded meanwhile; record then drops it (c < c+1) although the client is gone, resolve drops the client's nil entry because it is not live, and nothing is sent, so its cursor stays on the other processes until the 30 s expiry. Before e2a61748 that removal went out at c and was accepted.

The window-1 test (:352-418) runs its return from beforeAwarenessRemovalRead, before the single snapshot; at round-5 code that place was before GetStates, which already saw alice live, so the test passes with the bug (the tester's negative control moved the hook between the reads by hand). A return cannot land inside one locked EncodeUpdate; delete the test and the beforeAwarenessRemovalRead hook, or make it exercise a real window. The three window tests copy one body (:294-350, :363-417, :429-487); :278-289 still explains the race through Meta; :358 ends with a stray 'with'.
Comment errors: :221-222 'holds nothing older' should be 'holds no later clock'; :690-691 'what neither read sees' is wrong, the second read (Meta) saw the return's clock.
Size line was +16064/-4462; at 106f21e5 it is 127 files, +16031/-4429. The reviewer corrected it in the body (no push).

verified: Window 1 closed: touched decides each removal from one aw.EncodeUpdate snapshot (ygo RLock, awareness.go:458-482); a live state skips the removal.
Lock order: touched releases r.mu before aw.Meta and EncodeUpdate; record takes r.mu only; no new nesting with ygo's awareness lock.
